summary: A one-person, open-source programming-font site built as a dark Vue single page: a gradient hero with a typed tagline, an editable code editor, a ligature on/off board, a wipe comparison against 23 other coding fonts, then donation, install, supporter, tweet, FAQ and credits sections under a fixed gradient nav. Everything is set in Victor Mono, and the cursive italic is used for headings and keywords.

instances.look: Name 'Victor Mono' at ~141px centred over a slowly shifting diagonal gradient (orange → magenta → violet, later teal → green) with a faint video of code being typed behind it; tagline 'The ___| programming font' and two outlined buttons 'Download' and 'Share'
instances.ux: The adjective in the tagline is typed and deleted in a loop in the cursive italic ('dashing', 'definite', 'delicate', '"#%§§##/'); Share opens a row of social icons; the fixed nav appears only after the hero
instances.learn: Type the swapping word of the tagline in the italic: the typing animation shows the special style before any specimen

reconstruction.layout: Full-width 1440×535 (≈60vh) header; name centred at y≈120–230, tagline centred ~70px below, button row centred ~60px under the tagline (two ~150×44px outlined buttons with 16px gap)
reconstruction.typography: Name ~141px Victor Mono Regular, light grey #eeeeee, normal tracking; tagline ~32px Regular with the changing word in Victor Mono Italic (cursive) followed by a blinking '|' cursor; buttons ~13px Regular with icon
reconstruction.behaviour: Granim.js canvas gradient (mix-blend-mode: screen) animates through colour states every few seconds; a muted looping MP4 of code being typed sits underneath at 50% opacity; Typed.js types and backspaces the tagline word in a loop
reconstruction.content: Name, a one-line positioning tagline whose adjective rotates, Download (ZIP) and Share
reconstruction.assets: Short looping video of code being typed (headerbg.mp4/webm); gradient stops for Granim
reconstruction.html: div.header > video.video-bg + canvas.header-gradients + div.text > h1 + h2 (em.property + span.typed-cursor) + buttons; span.share hidden with Twitter/Facebook/Reddit/Weibo icons

instances.look: 'Try it' heading in cursive italic above a slate-teal CodeMirror editor showing a ~20-line async JavaScript function with Oceanic Next syntax colours; comments and keywords like 'true' render in the cursive italic

instances.learn: For a coding font the most convincing tester is a real editor with a real theme, where the syntax highlighter decides where the italic appears

reconstruction.behaviour: Editable CodeMirror (theme oceanic-next); typing reflows normally; calt ligatures (=== → ≡ style) render in the editor
reconstruction.content: Real code: async getUser() loop with prompt, fetch, try/catch and comments; mobile shows a Vue single-file component starting '<!-- Go ahead and edit me -->'

instances.look: 'Ligatures' heading with a small outlined 'enabled' pill; below, every ligature sequence (</ </> ~> -> => === != <=> |> ++ +++ …) centred in six lines of arrows and symbols
instances.ux: Clicking the 'enabled' pill crossfades the block to an identical copy with ligatures off, so every sequence flips between symbol and raw characters at once
instances.learn: Stack two copies of the full ligature list (one with liga/calt off) and crossfade them: the whole catalogue becomes a single before/after

reconstruction.layout: Section ~520px; heading centred; ligature lines centred in a ~1080px column, ~45px line pitch, generous word spacing

reconstruction.behaviour: Two absolutely stacked h1 copies (.crossfade.visible / .crossfade.hidden.no-ligatures); the button swaps classes for an opacity crossfade
reconstruction.content: Every programming ligature in the font, space-separated

instances.look: 'Compare it to [JetBrains Mono ▾]' with a select of 23 coding fonts; below, a code screenshot split by a white vertical line with a round ◂▸ handle: Victor Mono on the left, the chosen rival on the right
